summary: Lili Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University (attested 2011) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.

Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel (~1938–1948) and Swami Lakshman Joo (1948). She held positions at the CNRS as Boursière (~1945–1948) and researcher (~1948–1978).

Lilla Russell-Smith specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London and studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós.
Lily de Silva worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Julius Berugoda (attested 1970) and M. Sri Rammandala, and held posts at the University of Ceylon (attested 1970 and 2008).

Limei Chi works in Buddhist studies and sinology and studied under Jinhua Chen. Chi held posts as faculty at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and Professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).
Lin He (1902–1992) was a philosopher who studied at Tsinghua University (~1919–1926). He later held a position at National Tsing Hua University from circa 1931 to 1937.
Lin Heng is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).
Lin Li works in the fields of computational studies and linguistics, and has held posts at Utrecht University and Qinghai Normal University.

Linda Hogan (born 1964) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Maynooth University and Trinity College Dublin. She held posts at Chester, Leeds, and Trinity College Dublin, including Vice-Provost and Chief Academic Officer (2011–2016).
Linda Jean LaMacchia works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the doctoral supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).
Linda Learman is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She was supervised by doctoral advisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory (both attested 2005).
Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993. She served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
Lindsay G. McCune specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. McCune studied under MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas as well as Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark (born 1932) is a scholar of sinology who served as professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay, and at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a sinologist who earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the doctoral supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo (attested 2014).

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1958–1964) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1968–1972), later holding a post at the University of Tartu (~1969–2010).

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist educated at Liverpool and Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), as Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1906–1917), and Lecturer at SOAS (1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia (born 1968) works in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Lille (1997). He held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University (attested 2002), and Lyon 2 (attested 2010–2014).

Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1944–1949), the State Council translation administration department, and the Ethnic Publishing House.

Lisa Grumbach specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She has held posts at Stanford University (attested 1996) and as an assistant professor (助教授) at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
